Build a library catalog application for a neighborhood reading group. The application should track books, copies, readers, loans, reservations and return dates. Begin with the existing catalog data format and preserve the stable identifiers in exported records. Make the work easy to review through the normal application entry point. Keep each part understandable without relying on project history or conversations that are unavailable to a new contributor.

The catalog page should show the title, author, publication year and available copy count for every book. Readers can filter by title or author and combine those filters with an availability switch. An empty result should explain that no books match the current filters. Clearing the filters should restore the complete list without discarding the selected sort order. Keyboard users should reach every control in a predictable order and see which control currently has focus.

The loan page should record which reader borrowed a copy and when it is due. Prevent two active loans from claiming the same copy. Returning a book should make it available immediately unless a reservation is waiting. A reservation should keep its place in the queue across an application restart. Show the next eligible reservation beside the returned copy so the librarian can complete the handoff without opening several unrelated pages.

Provide import and export commands for a small documented JSON format. The import command must report an invalid row with its record identifier and a useful explanation. Validate the complete input before writing any changes so a malformed final record cannot leave an incomplete catalog. Exported records should have a stable order and include enough information to reconstruct readers, copies and active loans in an empty installation. Document the expected encoding and date format.

Use a disposable fixture with several books, multiple copies of one title, an overdue loan and two readers waiting for the same copy. Exercise filtering, checkout, return and reservation handoff through the same functions the application calls. Include a restart between creating a reservation and returning its book. Confirm that the queue order and due date survive. Add an invalid import case and verify that the original catalog remains unchanged after the command reports the error.

Keep error messages short and describe the action the librarian can take. Explain how to start the application with the sample catalog and how to save an export before upgrading. Use relative example paths under a sample workspace. Run the build, static checks and focused tests for the catalog and command packages. Finish by describing the behavior visible on the catalog and loan pages and the commands used to verify that behavior.
